title: Constructing and characterising anharmonic potentials in a harmonic oscillator
summary: Continuous-variable quantum systems offer a natural platform for quantum information processing and analogue quantum simulation of real-world processes. Realising these applications, however, requires anharmonic potentials with programmable functional forms, which are challenging to engineer on demand. Here, in a superconducting harmonic oscillator coupled to a transmon qubit, we construct programmable non-Gaussian phase gates $e^{-iV(\hat{X})}$, corresponding to the impulsive action of an anharmonic potential $V(\hat{X})$, and characterise them by reconstructing their corresponding force…
